description: Environment-variable dispatch in namespace mode (PROTOCOL_SPEC 9.8.2 rules 3 and 4, decision D-146). Only the `apcore` namespace may use the exact prefix `APCORE` (CONFIG_NAMESPACE_RESERVED); a prefix that merely begins with `APCORE_` is legal. A variable is dispatched to ONE namespace, the longest matching prefix, and an `APCORE_` variable that matches no registered prefix belongs to `apcore`. Measured before D-146: all three SDKs accepted `APCORE` for any namespace; apcore-python and apcore-typescript applied every `APCORE_*` variable to the `apcore` namespace AND dispatched it by prefix, so `APCORE_MCP_TRANSPORT` landed in both `apcore-mcp.transport` and `apcore.mcp.transport`; apcore-rust wrote an unmatched `APCORE_` variable to a top-level path outside every namespace.

driver_contract.isolation: Start each case from a namespace registry holding only the framework's built-in namespaces, and with every environment variable beginning `APCORE` unset except those in `input.env`.
driver_contract.registration: Register each entry of `input.namespaces` with the SDK's public register_namespace, in order. When `expected.register_error_code` is present, the LAST registration MUST raise that code and nothing further is run.
driver_contract.load: Otherwise write `input.config_file` (a namespace-mode document) to a real file and load it with the SDK's Config loader, with `input.env` set.
driver_contract.values: `expected.values` maps a namespace-qualified dot-path (PROTOCOL_SPEC 9.9.1, first segment the namespace) to the value `Config.get` MUST return. `expected.absent` lists namespace-qualified dot-paths `Config.get` MUST report as absent (null / None / undefined).

test_cases.description: The over-correction guard: `APCORE_MCP` shares a leading string with `APCORE` and is legal (9.8.2 rule 2).
